title: Summary and Note-making
notes: **Summary:** read for gist → underline key ideas → draft (author's main idea first, then 2–4 key supports) → cut modifiers/examples to fit the word limit → verify meaning is unchanged and nothing is copied.

**Summary grammar:** four paraphrase moves — synonym swap (threat→danger), word-class change (pollute→pollution), voice change (active↔passive), sentence merge; report verbs frame it ('the passage argues…'). Never add your own opinion.

**Note-making:** TITLE in caps → numbered sub-headings (1, 2, 3 — noun phrases, one per paragraph) → compact key-phrase points (a, b, c) → abbreviations (&, →, e.g.) with an 'Abbreviations used' note.
**Note grammar:** nominalise verbs for headings ('agricultural expansion'); drop articles/auxiliaries in points; every point under 7 words.

mcqs.question: A common examiner point on "Summary and Note-making" is that a statement is only valid when its condition of applicability is met. Is that TRUE or FALSE?
mcqs.explanation: Every NEB rule has a scope (e.g. a specific range, temperature, or sign convention); stating the condition earns full marks.
